examples.en: In winter I want to eat frozen pollack stew.
I bought two frozen pollack at the market.
Mom put the frozen pollack in the fridge.
We often eat pollack jeon on holidays.
This restaurant's pollack soup is delicious.
You have to thaw frozen pollack first.

explain: 명태는 상태에 따라 이름이 달라져요. 얼린 것은 동태, 말린 것은 북어, 반쯤 말린 것은 코다리예요. 동태는 주로 찌개나 전으로 먹어요.
explain_en: Pollack changes its name depending on its state: frozen is 동태, dried is 북어, and half-dried is 코다리. 동태 is mostly eaten in stew (동태찌개) or as jeon (동태전).

examples.en: There was an accident, but he walked out unharmed.

examples.ko: 어제 아팠던 친구가 오늘은 멀쩡히 학교에 왔어요.
examples.en: My friend who was sick yesterday came to school today looking totally fine.

examples.ko: 잘 되던 컴퓨터가 멀쩡히 있다가 갑자기 꺼졌어요.
examples.en: The computer, which had been working fine, suddenly shut off.
Even though I dropped it, the phone turns on just fine.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말을 했어요.
examples.en: He sat there straight-faced and lied.
The child fell but got up fine and laughed.

explain: 멀쩡히는 다치거나 고장 날 것 같은 상황인데도 아무 문제가 없다는 느낌이 강해요. '멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말하다'처럼 뻔뻔한 태도를 탓할 때도 써요. 사고, 병, 고장 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 멀쩡히 stresses that something is fine even though you would expect harm or breakage. It is also used to blame shameless behavior, as in 멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말하다. It often appears in stories about accidents, illness, or breakdowns.

examples.en: Grasshoppers hop around the rice fields in autumn.
The children are catching grasshoppers.
Grasshoppers live on grass.

examples.ko: 메뚜기 한 마리가 내 어깨에 앉았어요.
examples.en: A grasshopper landed on my shoulder.
I heard people used to eat stir-fried grasshoppers.
Try jumping high like a grasshopper.

explain: 메뚜기는 곤충이지만 예전에는 가을에 볶아서 반찬으로 먹기도 했어요. 비슷하게 풀밭에서 보이는 곤충으로 방아깨비가 있고, 가을밤에 우는 곤충은 귀뚜라미예요.
explain_en: 메뚜기 is an insect, but people used to stir-fry it as a side dish in autumn. Another insect seen in grass is the 방아깨비, while the one that sings on autumn nights is the 귀뚜라미.

examples.en: The child laughs happily riding the wooden horse.
There is an old wooden horse at the playground.
Do you know the story of the Trojan horse?
My younger sibling rocked back and forth on the rocking horse.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 손자에게 나무 목마를 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandpa made a wooden toy horse for his grandson.
This rocking horse has been here since I was a baby.

explain: 목마는 말 모양 장난감이나 놀이기구 말에 써요. 아이를 어깨에 태우는 '목말'과 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리지만 서로 다른 말이에요. '트로이 목마'는 컴퓨터 바이러스 이야기에도 나와요.
explain_en: 목마 refers to a toy horse or a ride horse. It sounds close to 목말 (carrying a child on the shoulders), but they are different words. 트로이 목마 also appears in talk about computer viruses.

examples.en: You receive the question sheet when the test starts.
You must not doodle on the question sheet.
We were short of question sheets, so I made copies.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나면 답안지와 문제지도 같이 내요.
examples.en: When the test ends, you hand in the question sheet along with the answer sheet.
The print on this question sheet is too small.
Be sure to check the back of the question sheet too.

explain: 시험에서 문제가 적힌 종이는 문제지, 답을 쓰는 종이는 답안지예요. 연습으로 풀어 보는 종이는 보통 '학습지'라고 해요. 시험 때 주로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: In an exam, the sheet with the questions is 문제지 and the sheet you write answers on is 답안지. A sheet used for practice is usually called 학습지. The word is mainly used around tests.

examples.en: This painting is still unfinished.
Because it's an unfinished work, the price is different.
I submitted it while it was still incomplete.
If your homework is unfinished, hand it in by tomorrow.
He left behind an unfinished symphony.
This building is unfinished but already famous.

explain: 끝낸 것은 완성, 아직 덜 끝난 것은 미완성이에요. '미'는 '아직 ~하지 않은'을 나타내서 미성년, 미혼, 미정에도 붙어요. 보통 '미완성 작품', '미완성이다'로 써요.
explain_en: Something finished is 완성 and something not yet finished is 미완성. The prefix 미 means 'not yet' and also appears in 미성년, 미혼, and 미정. It is usually used as 미완성 작품 or 미완성이다.

examples.en: I bought a stand for the flower pot.
With a laptop stand, your neck feels better.
A statue stands on the pedestal.
I propped up the books with a support so they wouldn't fall.

examples.ko: 이 받침대는 높이를 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: The height of this stand can be changed.
Please set your phone upright on the stand.

explain: 받침대는 물건 밑에서 받쳐 주는 도구를 넓게 말해요. 휴대폰이나 태블릿을 세워 두는 것은 보통 '거치대', 컵 밑에 까는 것은 '컵받침'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 받침대 broadly means anything that props up an object from below. A holder that keeps a phone or tablet upright is usually called 거치대, and a coaster under a cup is 컵받침.

examples.en: You have to clean up your dog's waste on the street.
Animal waste smells strong.
I had a stool and urine test at the hospital.
My car got dirty because of bird droppings.

examples.ko: 화장실 청소는 배설물이 쌓이지 않게 자주 해야 해요.
examples.en: You should clean the bathroom often so waste doesn't pile up.

examples.ko: 배설물로 몸 상태를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell your health condition from your waste.

explain: 배설물은 대변과 소변을 함께 가리키는 말이라 의학, 동물, 위생 이야기에서 써요. 일상에서는 '똥', '오줌'이라고도 하지만 점잖게 말할 때는 배설물이 나아요.
explain_en: 배설물 covers both stool and urine, so it is used in medical, animal, and hygiene contexts. In daily talk people also say 똥 and 오줌, but 배설물 sounds more polite.

examples.en: I read this novel in the Korean translation.
The translation is easier than the original.
I found the English translation at the bookstore.
The title differs a little in each translation.

examples.ko: 번역본은 읽기는 쉽지만 느낌이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: A translation is easy to read, but the feel is a bit different.
My friend left notes in the translated copy.

explain: 번역하기 전의 글은 '원본'이나 '원서', 번역한 책은 번역본이에요. 외국어로 쓴 책은 보통 '원서'라고 불러요. '한국어판', '영어판'처럼 '판'을 붙여 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The text before translation is 원본 or 원서, and the translated book is 번역본. A book in a foreign language is usually called 원서. People also say 한국어판 or 영어판 by adding 판.

examples.en: We did community service activities at school.
You need to complete your service hours to graduate.
I go do community service every weekend.
During vacation I did community service at a nursing home.
The community service became a good experience.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 벌금 대신 사회봉사를 하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Instead of a fine, he was ordered to do community service.

explain: 사회봉사는 학교나 법원이 정한 시간을 채우는 느낌이 있어요. 스스로 하는 일은 '자원봉사'라고 해요. '사회봉사를 하다', '봉사 시간'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 사회봉사 often feels like hours required by a school or court. Work done by choice is called 자원봉사. It is used as 사회봉사를 하다 or 봉사 시간.

examples.en: The wind blows in from the southwest.
The southwestern region of Korea is famous for rice.
Keep going toward the southwest.
There are many islands along the southwest coast.
The sun is sinking toward the southwest.
My house is southwest of the school.

explain: 서남과 남서는 같은 방향이에요. 일기예보에서는 '남서풍'처럼 남서를 쓰고, 지역 이름에는 '서남해안'처럼 서남이 보여요. 같은 짝으로 동남과 남동이 있어요.
explain_en: 서남 and 남서 point to the same direction. Weather forecasts say 남서풍, while 서남 shows up in place names like 서남해안. 동남 and 남동 form a similar pair.

examples.ko: 절 마당에 오래된 석탑이 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old stone pagoda stands in the temple yard.
I looked at stone pagodas in Gyeongju.
They say this stone pagoda is over a thousand years old.
We took a photo in front of the stone pagoda.
Snow piled up on top of the stone pagoda.
I visited a temple famous for its stone pagoda.

explain: 탑은 재료에 따라 돌로 만든 석탑, 나무로 만든 목탑, 벽돌로 만든 전탑으로 나눠요. 한국은 석탑이 특히 많아요. 불국사의 석가탑과 다보탑이 대표적이에요.
explain_en: Pagodas are divided by material: 석탑 (stone), 목탑 (wood), and 전탑 (brick). Korea has especially many 석탑. 석가탑 and 다보탑 at Bulguksa are the best-known examples.

examples.en: Food got stuck and I nearly choked.
The doctor opened the patient's airway.

examples.ko: 월급이 들어와서 이번 달은 숨통이 좀 트였어요.
examples.en: My pay came in, so I have some breathing room this month.

examples.ko: 일이 너무 많아서 잠깐 쉬며 숨통을 틔웠어요.
examples.en: I had so much work that I took a short break to catch my breath.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 경쟁사 때문에 숨통이 조여 오고 있어요.
examples.en: That company is being squeezed hard by its competitor.
When I opened the window, I felt I could breathe again.

explain: 숨통은 숨 쉬는 길인데, '숨통이 트이다', '숨통을 조이다'처럼 비유로도 많이 써요. 의학에서는 '기관'이나 '기도'라고 해요.

phrases.en: to finally get some breathing room
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들고 답답하던 상황이 풀려서 한숨 돌릴 때 써요. 돈, 일, 시간 모두에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a tight or stressful situation eases and you can finally relax a bit. It works for money, work, or time.

explain_en: 숨통 is the passage for breathing, and it is also widely used figuratively, as in 숨통이 트이다 or 숨통을 조이다. In medicine the terms are 기관 or 기도.

examples.en: The wound has already healed.
The injured spot is slowly healing.
It heals faster if you put medicine on it.
The wound healed, so I took off the bandage.
It takes time for a wound to close up.
Emotional wounds don't heal easily.

explain: 아물다는 갈라진 상처가 붙어서 나아지는 것이고, 병이 나을 때는 '낫다'를 써요. 상처가 더 나빠지는 것은 '덧나다'라고 해요. ㄹ이 빠져서 '아문 상처', '아무니까'처럼 활용돼요.
explain_en: 아물다 is for a split wound closing up, while 낫다 is used for recovering from illness. When a wound gets worse it is 덧나다. The ㄹ drops, giving forms like 아문 상처 and 아무니까.

examples.en: Under the moonlight the lake sparkles silver.
The grandmother with silvery hair is smiling.
The fish's scales are silver.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 은빛 드레스를 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: The actress appeared in a silver dress.
A silvery field of snow spread out on the winter morning.
Silver feels calmer than gold.

explain: 은빛은 반짝이는 은색 빛이라서 달빛, 눈, 물결, 흰머리를 예쁘게 표현할 때 좋아요. 짝이 되는 말은 '금빛'이에요. 흰머리를 멋지게 말할 때는 '은발'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: 은빛 is silver with a shimmer, so it suits moonlight, snow, ripples, and gray hair. Its counterpart is 금빛. Gray hair can also be called 은발 in a flattering way.

examples.en: Green moss has grown on the rock.
When it rains, you slip on moss.
Moss grows well in shady places.
I went down the mossy stone steps carefully.
I put a pot decorated with moss in the garden.
I walked along a forest path that smelled of moss.

explain: 이끼는 '이끼가 끼다'처럼 끼다와 짝으로 쓰고, 오래되고 축축한 곳을 떠올리게 해요. '구르는 돌에는 이끼가 끼지 않는다'는 속담도 있어요.
explain_en: 이끼 pairs with 끼다 as in 이끼가 끼다 and suggests old, damp places. There is a proverb, 구르는 돌에는 이끼가 끼지 않는다.

examples.en: Carp swim in the pond.
I fed the carp at the park.
Carp are fish that live a long time.
My grandfather likes carp fishing.
I saw a big carp at the market.
They say braised carp is good for your health.

explain: 잉어는 민물고기이고, 색이 화려한 관상용 잉어는 '비단잉어'라고 해요. 모양이 비슷한 붕어와 달리 잉어는 입가에 수염이 있어요.
explain_en: 잉어 is a freshwater fish, and the colorful ornamental kind is called 비단잉어. Unlike the similar-looking 붕어, 잉어 has barbels at the corners of its mouth.

examples.ko: 제트기가 큰 소리를 내며 하늘을 날았어요.
examples.en: A jet flew through the sky with a loud roar.
A jet is much faster than an ordinary plane.
I saw a private jet at the airport.

examples.ko: 이 제트기는 열 명만 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only ten people can ride this jet.
Since I was little, my dream was to be a jet pilot.
At the exhibition I climbed aboard an old jet.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '비행기'라고 하고, 제트기는 제트 엔진을 단 빠른 비행기를 따로 말할 때 써요. 싸우는 군용 비행기는 '전투기', 사람을 태우는 큰 비행기는 '여객기'예요.
explain_en: In daily life people just say 비행기, and 제트기 is used when specifically meaning a fast plane with a jet engine. A military fighting plane is a 전투기 and a large passenger plane is a 여객기.

examples.en: The manager of our bank branch is very kind.
The branch manager greeted the staff.
There is a gathering to introduce the new branch manager.
I'm busy because there is a branch managers' meeting today.
I inquired directly with the branch manager.

examples.ko: 형은 입사 십 년 만에 지점장이 됐어요.
examples.en: My older brother became a branch manager ten years after joining.

explain: 한 가게의 주인은 '사장님', 한 지점의 책임자는 '지점장님'이라고 불러요. 회사 전체를 이끄는 사람은 '대표'예요. 은행, 보험사, 체인점에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: The owner of a shop is 사장님, while the person in charge of one branch is 지점장님. The person leading the whole company is the 대표. You hear it often at banks, insurers, and chain stores.

examples.en: There is an old typewriter in Grandpa's room.
The author wrote the novel on a typewriter.
The sound of the typewriter echoed in the quiet room.

examples.ko: 요즘은 타자기를 쓰는 사람이 거의 없어요.
examples.en: These days almost nobody uses a typewriter.
I tried typing on an old typewriter at the museum.

examples.ko: 타자기는 글자를 하나 틀리면 고치기 어려워요.
examples.en: On a typewriter, one wrong letter is hard to fix.

explain: 컴퓨터로 글자를 치는 일도 '타자를 치다'라고 하는데, 타자기를 쓰던 때의 표현이 그대로 남은 거예요. 지금은 영화나 박물관에서 타자기를 더 자주 보고, '타자 속도'라는 말은 아직 써요.
explain_en: Typing on a computer is still called 타자를 치다, an expression left over from the days of the 타자기. Today you see a 타자기 mostly in movies or museums, but 타자 속도 (typing speed) is still used.

examples.en: Twins seem to have telepathy.

examples.ko: 둘이 똑같은 말을 해서 텔레파시인 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: We said the exact same thing, so I thought it was telepathy.

examples.ko: 텔레파시로 생각을 보낼 수 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish I could send thoughts by telepathy.
The hero in the movie uses telepathy.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 네 생각을 했는데 텔레파시가 통했나 봐요.
examples.en: I thought of you last night, so maybe we connected by telepathy.

examples.ko: 그 둘은 말 안 해도 텔레파시처럼 알아요.
examples.en: Those two understand each other like telepathy without speaking.

explain: 텔레파시는 외래어이고, 마음이 서로 통한다는 뜻의 '이심전심'과 느낌이 비슷해요. '텔레파시가 통하다'로 많이 쓰고, 친구나 가족이 같은 생각을 했을 때 농담처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 텔레파시 is a loanword, and it feels close to the four-character phrase 이심전심 (hearts understanding each other). People say 텔레파시가 통하다, often jokingly when friends or family think the same thing.

examples.en: I commute by subway.

examples.ko: 매일 한 시간씩 통근하는 게 힘들어요.
examples.en: Commuting an hour every day is hard.
The office was far, so I commuted by bus.

examples.ko: 회사 가까이로 이사하면 통근할 때 편해요.
examples.en: If you move closer to your workplace, commuting is easier.
I used to commute by car, but now I go by bicycle.
I commute from Seoul to Incheon.

explain: 출근은 일하러 가는 것, 퇴근은 일을 마치고 가는 것, 통근은 집과 직장을 오가는 것 전체예요. 말할 때는 '출근해요'를 더 많이 쓰고 통근하다는 글과 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 회사 버스는 '통근 버스'라고 해요.
explain_en: 출근 is going to work, 퇴근 is leaving after work, and 통근 is the whole trip between home and work. In speech 출근해요 is more common, while 통근하다 appears often in writing and news. A company shuttle is a 통근 버스.

examples.en: The brain uses glucose as energy.
I got a glucose injection at the hospital.
Glucose is found in fruit and honey.

examples.ko: 피곤할 때 포도당 사탕을 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people eat glucose candy when they're tired.

examples.ko: 피 속 포도당이 너무 높으면 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If the glucose in your blood is too high, you should go to the hospital.

examples.ko: 혈당 검사는 피 속 포도당 양을 재는 거예요.
examples.en: A blood sugar test measures the amount of glucose in your blood.

explain: 일상에서 '당'은 단맛 나는 것 전체를 말하고, 포도당은 그중 몸이 에너지로 쓰는 한 종류예요. 병원에서는 포도당이 든 수액을 놓고, 피 속 포도당 수치는 '혈당'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily life 당 refers to sweet things in general, and 포도당 is the one kind your body uses for energy. Hospitals give 수액 containing 포도당, and the glucose level in blood is called 혈당.

examples.en: I rode the carousel at the amusement park.
The kids say they like the carousel best.
The carousel turns slowly, so it isn't scary.

examples.ko: 회전목마 앞에 줄이 길게 서 있어요.
examples.en: There is a long line in front of the carousel.

examples.ko: 회전목마에서 내리자마자 또 타고 싶다고 했어요.
examples.en: As soon as she got off the carousel, she said she wanted another ride.
At night the lights come on at the carousel and it looks pretty.

explain: 놀이공원에서 가장 순한 놀이기구를 말할 때 자주 나와요. 무서운 놀이기구는 '롤러코스터'나 '바이킹'이라고 하고, 회전목마는 어린아이도 탈 수 있어요.
explain_en: 회전목마 comes up as the gentlest ride at an amusement park. Scary rides are called 롤러코스터 or 바이킹, while even small children can ride a 회전목마.

examples.en: The relay race is the most fun at sports day.
Our class took first place in the relay race.
I was the last runner of the relay.
I dropped the baton during the relay.
I watched the Olympic relay on television.
In a relay, teammates must be in sync to be fast.

explain: 계주와 이어달리기는 같은 경기예요. 계주는 한자어이고 이어달리기는 순우리말이에요. 넘겨 주는 막대는 '바통'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 계주 and 이어달리기 are the same event. 계주 is a Sino-Korean word and 이어달리기 is a native Korean word. The stick that is passed is called a 바통.

examples.en: This singer has a wide repertoire.
The pianist is preparing a new repertoire.
My father's repertoire of stories is always the same.
I added a Korean song to the repertoire too.
My cooking repertoire has grown a lot too.
Today's concert program is all classical.

explain: 공연에서는 연주나 노래할 수 있는 작품 목록을 말하고, 일상에서는 늘 하는 이야기나 농담을 비유할 때도 써요. 노래방에서 가장 자신 있는 노래는 '십팔번'이라고 해요. 표준 표기는 '레퍼토리'예요.
explain_en: On stage 레퍼토리 is the list of works a performer can play or sing, and in daily life it can describe someone's usual stories or jokes. The song you are best at in karaoke is called 십팔번. The standard spelling is 레퍼토리.

examples.en: I feel a great sense of satisfaction after finishing the work.
Customer satisfaction matters too.
I feel satisfied in my new home.

examples.ko: 높은 점수가 주는 만족감은 오래가지 않아요.
examples.en: The satisfaction from a high score doesn't last long.
Her face lit up with satisfaction.

examples.ko: 그는 만족감으로 가득 찬 얼굴로 웃었어요.
examples.en: He smiled with a face full of satisfaction.

explain: 만족은 '만족해요'처럼 마음에 든다고 말할 때 쓰고, 만족감은 그때 드는 느낌 자체를 말해요. '만족감을 느끼다/주다/높이다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요. '뿌듯함'은 해냈다는 자랑스러움이 더 들어 있어요.
explain_en: 만족 is used to say you are pleased, as in 만족해요, while 만족감 names the feeling itself. It pairs with verbs like 만족감을 느끼다, 주다, and 높이다. 뿌듯함 carries more of a proud feeling of having achieved something.

examples.en: You need to watch your words in front of elders.
Even between friends, watching your words is a must.
You have to watch what you say in front of a child.

examples.ko: 말조심에 신경 쓰다 보니 대화가 어색해졌어요.
examples.en: Because I was careful about what I said, the conversation became awkward.
Watching your words is also a habit.

examples.ko: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다니까 말조심이 필요해요.
examples.en: Daytime words are heard by birds and nighttime words by mice, so you need to watch your words.

explain: 말조심은 '말조심을 하다', '말조심이 필요하다'처럼 쓰는 명사예요. 짧게 '말조심!'이라고 하면 화가 난 경고로 들릴 수 있어요. 점잖게 말할 때는 '말을 가려서 하세요'가 좋아요.
explain_en: 말조심 is a noun used in patterns like 말조심을 하다 and 말조심이 필요하다. Said bluntly as 말조심!, it can sound like an angry warning. A politer way is 말을 가려서 하세요.

en: watch one's words; be careful what one says

examples.en: You have to watch what you say at work.
Please be careful with your words in front of elders.
Even though I was angry, I should have watched my words.
He is being careful with his words in front of reporters.
If you don't watch your words, misunderstandings happen.
Many people watch their words on social media too.

explain: '말조심하세요'는 친절한 충고도 되지만, 짧은 '말조심해!'는 화가 난 경고로 들릴 수 있어요. 친구에게 부드럽게 말할 때는 '조심해서 말해 줘'가 편해요.
explain_en: 말조심하세요 can be friendly advice, but the short 말조심해! can sound like an angry warning. To a friend, a softer way is 조심해서 말해 줘.

examples.en: The specialty of this market is hotteok.
Gyeongju bread is a famous specialty of Gyeongju.
That bridge has become a landmark of the city.

examples.ko: 여행 가면 지역 명물을 꼭 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: When I travel, I always try the local specialty.
It's the famous grandma's tteokbokki place in our neighborhood.
I went to a restaurant famed as a local attraction.

explain: 명물은 그곳에 가면 꼭 보거나 먹어야 하는 유명한 것을 말해서 음식뿐 아니라 건물, 사람에게도 써요. 지역에서 나는 물건은 '특산물', 대표 음식은 '대표 음식'이라고 하는 것이 더 정확해요.
explain_en: 명물 means a famous thing you must see or eat in a place, so it is used for buildings and people as well as food. Goods produced in a region are 특산물, and a signature dish is called 대표 음식.

examples.en: International students go back to their home country during vacation.

examples.ko: 모국을 떠난 지 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been ten years since I left my homeland.
I received a letter sent from my home country.
Even living abroad, I'm curious about news from my homeland.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 모국을 위해 열심히 뛰었어요.
examples.en: The athlete ran hard for his homeland.
One's homeland is always a place one misses.

explain: 모국은 외국에 사는 사람이 자기 나라를 그리워하며 말할 때 자주 써요. '고국'도 거의 같은 말이고, 자기가 처음 배운 말은 '모국어'라고 해요. 한국 사람이 일상에서 자기 나라를 말할 때는 '우리나라'가 가장 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 모국 is often used by people living abroad when they speak of their own country with longing. 고국 is almost the same, and the language you first learned is called 모국어. When Koreans talk about their own country in everyday speech, 우리나라 is the most natural.

examples.ko: 축구 경기 중에 선수들이 몸싸움을 했어요.
examples.en: The players scuffled during the soccer match.
A scuffle broke out on the subway.
Let's settle it with words before it gets physical.
In basketball the jostling under the basket is intense.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 몸싸움 끝에 경찰서에 갔어요.
examples.en: The two ended up at the police station after a scuffle.
The game ended without any scuffles.

explain: 몸싸움은 말다툼과 달리 몸이 부딪치는 싸움이에요. 크게 때리는 '주먹다짐'보다는 가볍고, 스포츠에서는 몸을 부딪치며 겨루는 것을 말할 때도 써요. '몸싸움을 벌이다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: 몸싸움 is a fight with bodily contact, unlike a verbal argument. It is milder than 주먹다짐 (a fistfight), and in sports it can also describe jostling for position. It is often used as 몸싸움을 벌이다.

examples.en: Minors need a guardian's consent form.
Underage students need their parents' permission.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 미성년자가 볼 수 없어요.
examples.en: Minors cannot watch this movie.

examples.ko: 미성년일 때는 혼자 계약할 수 없어요.
examples.en: While underage, you cannot sign a contract alone.
I take care of my younger sibling, who is a minor.
There is safety education for minors.

explain: 한국에서는 만 19세 미만이 미성년이고, 사람을 말할 때는 '미성년자'를 더 자주 써요. 반대말은 '성년'이나 '성인'이고, 일상 말로는 '어른'이에요. 청소년은 따로 9세에서 24세 사이를 가리키는 법적 용어라 범위가 달라요.
explain_en: In Korea, a person under 19 (international age) is 미성년, and 미성년자 is more common for the person. The opposites are 성년 and 성인, or casually 어른. 청소년 is a separate legal term covering ages 9 to 24, so the range differs.

examples.en: Firefly lights glimmered on a country summer night.
The children ran off to see the firefly lights.

examples.ko: 반딧불은 깨끗한 곳에서만 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see firefly lights only in clean places.
Small lights came on one by one like fireflies.
I went to Muju to see the firefly festival.
Dozens of firefly lights blink in the forest.

explain: 반딧불은 반딧불이가 내는 빛이고, 곤충은 '반딧불이'라고 해요. 둘의 소리가 거의 같아서 문장에서 구분해 들어야 해요. 옛날에는 '개똥벌레'라고도 했어요.
explain_en: 반딧불 is the light a firefly makes, while the insect itself is 반딧불이. The two sound almost the same, so you must tell them apart in context. Long ago the insect was also called 개똥벌레.

examples.en: We take the exam in the library annex.
The annex is behind the main building.
The meeting is held on the third floor of the annex.
A new restaurant opened in the annex.
Please enter through the annex entrance instead of the main building.
Please tell me the way to the annex.

explain: 별관은 중심 건물 옆에 따로 지은 건물이고, 중심 건물은 '본관'이라고 해요. '신관'이나 '동관'처럼 이름이 붙은 건물도 많아요. 학교, 병원, 호텔에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 별관 is a building built separately beside the main one, which is called 본관. Buildings also carry names like 신관 or 동관. You see these at schools, hospitals, and hotels.

examples.ko: 그는 본업이 의사이고 취미로 노래를 해요.
examples.en: His main job is doctor, and he sings as a hobby.
These days my side job is busier than my main job.
I couldn't rest because I focused on my main job.
Singing is his main job, but he also acts.
I quit my main job and opened a shop.
It's hard to do my main job and child care together.

explain: 본업은 부업과 짝으로 쓰는 말이고, 가장 중심이 되는 직업이에요. 학생에게는 '본분'이라는 말을 써서 공부가 본분이라고 해요. 직업을 물을 때는 '본업이 뭐예요?'보다 '무슨 일을 하세요?'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 본업 pairs with 부업 (side job) and means the central occupation. For students people use 본분, saying that studying is their 본분. When asking someone's job, 무슨 일을 하세요? sounds more natural than 본업이 뭐예요?

en: inside the bones; marrow; deep down

examples.en: The cold wind cut right into my bones.
It's a day so cold it chills you to the bone.
The doctor said an infection has developed inside the bone.
Those words stayed with me deep down.
He is a Seoulite through and through.
That child is a prankster to the core.

explain: 뼛속은 실제로는 뼈 안쪽이지만 일상에서는 '뼛속까지 춥다'처럼 아주 깊고 강한 느낌을 말해요. '골수팬'의 '골수'는 뼈 안의 골수(骨髓)에서 온 말이라서, 마음 깊이 열성적인 팬을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: to be something to the core
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습만이 아니라 성격과 습관까지 완전히 그렇다는 뜻이에요. 사람의 성격이나 직업, 출신을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone is that way not just on the surface but in character and habits. Used for a person's nature, job, or background.
phrases.en_equiv: to the core; through and through

explain_en: 뼛속 literally means the inside of a bone, but in daily speech it conveys something deep and intense, as in 뼛속까지 춥다. The 골수 in 골수팬 (a die-hard fan) comes from bone marrow (骨髓), so it refers to a fan devoted deep down.

examples.en: After graduating I want to work at an industrial company.
Industry and the school do research together.
I went on a field internship at an industrial site.
There are many industrial companies in this area.
We need education that matches what industry wants.
Industry changes faster than schools.

explain: 산업체는 학교나 연구소와 구분해서, 물건을 만들고 파는 회사들을 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요. 뉴스나 학교 글에서 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 그냥 '회사'나 '공장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 산업체 groups together the companies that make and sell things, as opposed to schools or research institutes. It appears often in news and school writing, while in daily talk people just say 회사 or 공장.

examples.en: I got tax documents at the tax office.
You have to go to the tax office to register a business.
The tax office opens at nine on weekdays.
The tax office is close to my home.
A tax office employee explained kindly.
I have to send the documents to the tax office.

explain: 세무서는 세금을 걷고 신고를 받는 곳이에요. 신고를 대신해 주는 사람은 '세무사'라서 서로 달라요. 요즘은 '홈택스'로 인터넷에서도 신고해요. 주소나 증명서 일은 '구청'이나 '주민센터'에서 해요.
explain_en: 세무서 is where taxes are collected and returns are filed. The person who files for you is a 세무사, which is different. These days people also file online through 홈택스. Address and certificate matters go to the 구청 or 주민센터.

examples.en: A rooster crowed loudly at dawn.
Roosters are bigger than hens.
We raise a rooster in the yard.
A rooster climbed onto the roof.
I saw a rooster and hens at the farm.
Try waking up early like a rooster.

explain: 수탉은 수컷 닭이고 반대말은 '암탉'이에요. 암수를 가리지 않거나 고기를 말할 때는 그냥 '닭'이라고 해요. 닭의 울음소리는 '꼬끼오'라고 표현해요.
explain_en: 수탉 is a male chicken and its opposite is 암탉. When sex doesn't matter, or when speaking of the meat, people just say 닭. A rooster's crow is written as 꼬끼오.

examples.en: I use this expression often in real life.
I solved problems connected to real life.
I learned how math is used in real life.
I study practical English conversation.
Real life is very different from books.

examples.ko: 실생활에 도움이 되는 정보를 알려 줘요.
examples.en: They share information that helps in daily life.

explain: 실생활은 책이나 이론과 구분해서 진짜 살아가는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 일상생활과 비슷하지만, 배운 것이 실제로 쓰이느냐를 말하는 느낌이 더 강해요. '실생활 영어', '실생활에서 쓰다'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 실생활 is used to contrast real living with books or theory. It is close to 일상생활, but it leans more toward whether what you learned is actually used. It shows up often in phrases like 실생활 영어 and 실생활에서 쓰다.

examples.en: Carbohydrates are the body's source of energy.
Solar power is drawing attention as a clean energy source.
We are looking for a new energy source.
Breakfast becomes the energy source for the day.
Energy sources differ by country.
My children's laughter is what energizes me.

explain: 에너지원은 힘이 나오는 근원이라서 몸 이야기(탄수화물, 지방)와 전기를 만드는 자원(석유, 태양)에 모두 써요. 사람에게는 '힘이 되는 존재'를 비유로 말할 때도 써요. 연료는 태우는 물질에 쓰고 에너지원은 더 넓게 써요.
explain_en: 에너지원 is the origin of power, so it covers both the body (탄수화물, 지방) and resources for making electricity (석유, 태양). It can also describe a person who gives you strength. 연료 is for things that burn, while 에너지원 is broader.

examples.en: The wedding banquet hall is in the hotel basement.
The guests gathered in the banquet hall.
The banquet hall was full of music.

examples.ko: 연회장을 예약하려면 한 달 전에 연락하세요.
examples.en: To book a banquet hall, contact them a month in advance.
The year-end party is held in the banquet hall.
I'm looking for a hotel with a large banquet hall.

explain: 연회장은 피로연이나 송년회처럼 많은 사람이 모여 식사하는 큰 홀을 말해요. 결혼식을 올리는 곳은 '예식장'이라고 해서 연회장과 구분해요. 호텔에서는 '볼룸'이라고도 불러요.
explain_en: 연회장 is a large hall where many people gather to eat, such as for a wedding reception or a year-end party. The place where the wedding ceremony is held is called 예식장, which is different. Hotels sometimes call it a 볼룸.

en: stretching out repeatedly in long motions; smoothly and fast; growing fast

examples.en: I stretch my arms out in long strokes while stretching.
The child shot up in height.
I ran at full stride and arrived first.
It was hot, so I gulped down the juice.
The highway stretches out long and straight.

examples.ko: 책을 쭉쭉 읽다 보니 벌써 마지막 쪽이에요.
examples.en: I kept reading without stopping and I'm already on the last page.

explain: 쭉은 한 번에 길게 가는 느낌이고, 쭉쭉은 그 동작이 계속 이어지거나 막힘없이 진행되는 느낌이에요. 몸을 펴거나, 키가 크거나, 술술 읽고 달릴 때 써요. 식물이나 아이가 빨리 자랄 때는 '쑥쑥'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: 쭉 gives a feeling of going long in one stroke, and 쭉쭉 adds that the action continues or proceeds without a hitch. It is used for stretching the body, growing tall, or reading and running smoothly. For plants or children growing fast, 쑥쑥 is also very common.
